applicable_when: The kernel has xnumel=9 but XBLOCK=128, meaning 119 of 128 threads in the X dimension are masked out — 93% waste per block. The grid is (1, 4096), producing 4096 CTAs on 132 SMs = 1 full wave + 1 partial wave, where the partial wave accounts for up to 50% of runtime (LaunchConfiguration rule). Reducing XBLOCK to 1 (or a small value <= 9) and increasing YBLOCK to 32-128 will: (1) eliminate wasted masked threads, (2) increase the number of useful Y-dimension tiles per block improving occupancy, (3) reduce the partial-wave tail by reshaping the grid. Using @triton.autotune lets the runtime find the optimal tile shape across multiple configurations.
